title: Chapter 2911 - 162: Great Earth "Major" Formation _2
content:
Chapter 2911: Chapter 162: Great Earth "Major" Formation _2

If the Large Formation is truly destroyed, it would be equivalent to tearing down Uncle’s arrangement right under his nose, dismantling his game.

Mo Hua truly didn’t dare.

Moreover, he feared that if he blatantly ruined Uncle’s Large Formation, enraging him, some even more terrifying things might happen.

At the current stage, the famine disaster for the Barbaric Wilderness is akin to a calamity.

But Mo Hua knew that for Uncle, this was already a very "mild" approach.

If Uncle truly got angry and Gui Tao descended, at this moment the Barbaric Wilderness might all become "puppets" of Gui Tao’s people, with not a single living person left.

Mo Hua also didn’t know why Uncle didn’t go all out.

It might be that Uncle has other plots. Or perhaps Uncle is secretly competing with the Hua family or certain ancestors of the Taoist Court.

Mo Hua cannot fully comprehend the true grand scheme due to limited perspective.

But regardless, at this moment one cannot disrupt the game too much, lest it provokes those making the moves, personally stir up a bloody storm.

The situation in the Barbaric Wilderness, just stabilized a bit, simply cannot withstand these changes.

Thus, while Uncle is still "mild," and the aristocratic family’s attention isn’t completely focused on the Barbaric Wilderness yet, it’s necessary to suppress the famine disaster in a relatively low-profile manner.

Mo Hua pondered deeply and constructed many plans, eventually choosing to rebuild the Formation with Thick Earth Formation.

This way, without destroying the Famine Disaster Formation, through the Thick Earth Formation, providing a path of survival for all beings of the Barbaric Wilderness.

Using the vitality of Thick Earth to suppress the death qi of the famine disaster, thus barely achieving a balance between "life" and "death" in the Great Wilderness according to the heavenly secret setup.

And strictly speaking, this Thick Earth Formation cannot be considered a true "Large Formation."

Because a true "Large Formation" is too difficult, Mo Hua currently hasn’t the capability to fully "create" a genuine Large Formation.

This far exceeds his capability range.

Furthermore, the terrain and setup of the Barbaric Wilderness are also unsuitable for building a proper Large Formation.

Because the divisions of the Barbaric Wilderness are too chaotic.

Various Mountain Realms are intertwined, with differing grades, steep and rugged mountains, secluded paths, and many treacherous swamps and miasma...

Flattening the terrain, building a foundation, spanning mountains, and connecting the territories to build a Large Formation is almost impossible given the current manpower and resources.

Even if it were possible to build, it would take too long.

By the time the Large Formation is completed, the people of the Barbaric Wilderness would all have died.

Considering all these factors, Mo Hua can only, according to his capabilities and the specific, objective, and practical circumstances, adapt to the situation and construct a Thick Earth "Large" Formation.

Furthermore, one must consider the practical difficulty and consumption of building the Large Formation, as well as the learning and understanding abilities of the Witch Cultivators regarding relevant formations in the Great Wilderness.

Even the number of Witch Cultivators and the speed of the Drawing Formation must be considered.

The progress of the Large Formation must be compressed tightly enough...

The "test" itself is extraordinarily difficult, and the "examiner" is eerily terrifying.

There is no standard answer, not even a reference answer.

Moreover, there are so many complicated, redundant, and harsh "restriction" conditions...

Mo Hua naturally cannot design a real "Large Formation," and a real "Large Formation" would not solve the current problem.

After expending time and effort, Mo Hua ultimately came up with a "pseudo-Large Formation."

It has the scale of a Large Formation but lacks its structure.

The formations are interconnected, but unlike other Large Formations, does not have a "general control" Formation Pivot.

No "general formation eye" was constructed either.

Adhering to a "practical" mindset, Mo Hua erased all formal constraints according to the circulation of the laws, using only the simplest framework to achieve the most practical effect.

Thus, in the whole view, what Mo Hua built, rather than a "Large Formation," it was more like a large-scale assemblage of formations and a "hodgepodge."

Ordinary Formation Masters seeing this would determine it to be non-conformist, not standardized, a "heterodox sect," lacking inheritance and systematic rules.

But Mo Hua understood that all formation forms are carriers of Dao Laws.

Formations have no fixed form, and the law has no fixed law.

This is almost currently, under the Great Wilderness examination paper, and under the "famine disaster" test, the most perfect "answer sheet" a Formation Master could produce.

Unfortunately, no one can understand his answer.

Nor does anyone know what a harsh "exam" he is facing.

Not only do they not understand, but he’ll also face doubts and opposition.

...

At Vermilion Bird Mountain, in the ancient council hall.

Now, almost all the high-ranked Great Chiefs, Chief Elders, current chieftain chiefs, influential elders, and Barbarian Tribes generals from various tribes unanimously opposed and tried tirelessly to dissuade the construction of this Large Formation.

They did not understand why the Shaman here and now wanted to exhaust manpower and resources, construct such a costly Tao cultivation project.

——In a certain sense, this implied exhausting the foundation of a Mountain Realm to build this inexplicable "Holy Pattern" Large Formation.

This is a year of disaster, a year of turmoil.

The entire Vermilion Bird Mountain Realm just recovered from a brutal death battle with the Wujiu Tribe, now immediately wants to do such a foundation-exhausting act, truly baffling.

"The problem of the famine disaster is indeed dire, the decline of tribes and the sharp reduction of Barbarian Cultivators..."

"But the spread of the famine disaster has now halted, and major parts of the Vermilion Bird Mountain Realm, many tribes, have ultimately survived."

"Next, storing resources, saving grain, and patiently enduring through this famine disaster, we can still continue to grow and prosper."
